messages:
sara_support: FYI customer `acme-media` reporting a spike of 5xx/gateway timeouts to our hosted inference API since ~09:10 UTC. They say ~25% of calls failing, mostly short LLM completions (<=128 tokens). Errors: 504 gateway timeout and occasional 502 from model proxy.

luis_oncall: Acknowledge — paging SRE + runtime. Do we have a runbook link? :rotating_light: https://redwood/guides/incidents/autoscaling

autoscale-bot: HPA event: scale-to-0 inhibited by minReplicas=2; currentReplicas=2; desiredReplicas=8; timestamp=2024-07-20T09:15:12Z

alex_sre: Looking at metrics now. Grafana: /d/redwood/inference?panel=autoscale — spike in RPS at 09:11, CPU for runtime pods jumped and requests queue length climbed. KEDA scaler logs show missed triggers starting 09:12.

june_runtime: I see a bunch of pods entering `ImagePullBackOff` and long `Init` durations in the runtime cluster in us-east-1. Also model loader logs show ~40s to load model sharded checkpoint for the 13B variant — warmup time matters.

matt_devex: Customer repro steps? sara_support, can you paste a curl of a failing request (sanitized) so we can reproduce?

sara_support: Sent via DM, but here's an anonymized curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-open","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":64}'` Response: 504 after ~30s, no body except gateway timeout from edge.

alex_sre: Edge returns 504 when backend takes too long or upstream connection reset. Looking at envoy logs: repeated `upstream connect timeout` to runtime service endpoints around 09:13-09:18. K8s events show HPA wanted 8 but KEDA polling interval is 30s and scaler failed to scale because metrics-server was returning 503 for ~90s earlier.

luis_oncall: So chain: metrics-server blip -> KEDA misses scaler -> desired replicas higher than current -> pods start but slow warmup/model load -> requests queue -> gateway times out. Agrees?

june_runtime: Yes. Also saw readinessProbe failing for the runtime container until model loaded. Readiness probe is `http GET /ready` which checks KV cache warm and model loaded; in worst case that takes 35-50s, so pod not marked ready (won't receive traffic) until done. That prolongs the ramp.

matt_devex: Quick mitigation suggestions: 1) Increase HPA/KEDA minReplicas to keep warm pods 2) Add a pre-warmed pool (prefer warm pool in Dedicated, but for hosted we can increase min) 3) Reduce readiness gate to allow traffic and return 503 early while model loads (safer is a warmup endpoint) 4) Short-term: bump replicas manually to meet load.

luis_oncall: Oncall action: I'm going to manually scale the deployment to 6 replicas now to drain the queue.

autoscale-bot: kubectl scale deployment/inference-runtime --replicas=6 — accepted.

alex_sre: Scaling started. NOTE: image pulls still slow because of registry rate limits on some nodes — we should watch node saturation. Also the cluster autoscaler had a backlog; new nodes provisioning adds ~90s before pods schedule.

sara_support: Customer confirmed partial recovery at 09:28 - errors dropped to ~3%. They still see occasional 502s for larger prompts.

june_runtime: Created a temporary KEDA patch: reduce checkInterval=15s and cooldownPeriod=30s for the specific scaler for inference queue metric. Also increased minReplica to 3 for that scaler. Will deploy in 5 mins.

alex_sre: Logged short-term RCA: (1) metrics-server transient 503 caused KEDA missed scaling decisions; (2) readinessProbe gating on model load extended warmup; (3) node provisioning + image pulls added extra latency; (4) HPA minReplicas was too low for sudden spike.

matt_devex: Notes for long-term fixes: - Implement warm-pool / pre-warmed idle runtime pods with model pinned per popular models - Support async fast-fail responses with queued job acceptance token to avoid client 504s - Instrument KEDA metrics scrapes with alerting when scaler lag > 30s - Consider split of small/completion service with lightweight runtime for sub-128 token requests (faster startup).

luis_oncall: Actions taken: manual scale -> 6 replicas, KEDA config tweak deployed, increased minReplica to 3, added temporary alert on scaler_lag > 20s routed to oncall.

sara_support: I posted an incident update to customer: summary, mitigations, ETA for permanent fixes. They asked for a postmortem and whether we can assure this won't happen during their launch next week.

june_runtime: For postmortem we should gather: - KEDA scaler logs (/var/log/keda/keda-scaler.log) - metrics-server logs around 09:10-09:20 - model loader timings from runtime logs for redwood-13b-open - node provisioning events from cloud provider - envoy upstream errors.

alex_sre: Repro steps to simulate (dev cluster): 1) set HPA/KEDA minReplicas=2, reduce KEDA checkInterval to 30s, 2) spike RPS 3x with loadgen for 60s, 3) have model loader artificially sleep 30-45s, 4) observe queueing and 504s at edge. CLI snippet: ```bash
# spike
wrk2 -t4 -c200 -d60s --latency -s ./scripts/generate_load.lua http://dev-inference.internal/v1/generate
# simulate loader slowness
kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/inference-runtime MODEL_WARMUP_SLEEP=40
```

matt_devex: Also include a sample curl to reproduce 504s locally using a short timeout to mimic edge: `curl --max-time 20 -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-open","input":"x"}'`

luis_oncall: Next steps: run the repro in staging, measure time-to-ready for new pods with current readinessProbe, and propose changed readiness behaviour (graceful traffic ramp) by EOD. I'll file a P0 ticket to track changes.

sara_support: Customer updated: appreciate quick response, will monitor. They requested a timeline for 'warm pool' feature. I told them we'll follow up in the postmortem.

alex_sre: Tagging for the postmortem owners: @june_runtime (runtime), @matt_devex (product/short-term UX + API behavior), @sara_support (customer comms). I'll start drafting the timeline and add logs.

autoscale-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, summary='scale-up lag causing elevated 5xx during spike', incident_id=INC-2024-07-20-1012

sara_support: Thanks team. I'll close the customer ticket when postmortem is ready.

june_runtime: Adding one more: Consider adding a tiny `bootstrap` image that responds to readiness quickly and streams model weights asynchronously so pod can be ready faster (sketch in RFC).
